papers.title: A homotopical consequence of branched covers
papers.abstract: We prove that the profinite completion of a pseudomanifold is the Artin-Mazur's etale homotopy type construction on its branched covers, which was implicitly conjectured by Sullivan in his MIT note (page 272) around 1970. This is a consequence of the existence of enough $K(\pi,1)$ open dense subspaces in a pseudomanifold.

papers.title: The splitting of the stable space of equivariant $h$-cobordisms
papers.abstract: We prove that the space of equivariant $h$-cobordisms on a smooth $G$-manifold $M$ has a tom Dieck style splitting, after stabilization. As an intermediate step, we introduce a space of isovariant $h$-cobordisms on $M$ and prove that this space also has a splitting, even before stabilizing. This completes the proof of the equivariant version of Waldhausen's stable parametrized $h$-cobordism theorem. Along the way, we establish several foundational results on equivariant smooth manifolds with corners.

papers.title: Pure mapping class group fixed points in $\mathrm{PU}(2,1)$
papers.abstract: We classify all the fixed points for the action of the pure mapping class group on $\mathrm{PU}(2,1)$ character varieties of surface groups. Up to trivial peripheral monodromies, we prove that the irreducible fixed points are either pair of pants representations, or restrictions of reduced Burau representations to a once-punctured torus and restrictions of reduced Gassner representations to a 4-punctured sphere. On the other hand, we prove that the only non-trivial reducible fixed points appear in genus 0 where they map all but at most three peripheral loops in the centralizer of the image, and in genus 1 where they are valued in the quaternion group $H_8$. As consequences, we deduce (i) that an irreducible representation in genus 0 with at least four non-trivial peripheral monodromies is rigid if and only if it is a fixed point, and (ii) a partial classification of irreducible representations of pure braid groups into $\mathrm{PU}(2,1)$.

papers.title: On the Volume Conjectures for Dehn-filled $3$-manifolds along fundamental shadow link complements with big volume
papers.abstract: We prove the Volume Conjecture and the Asymptotic Expansion Conjecture for closed oriented hyperbolic $3$-manifolds obtained by integral Dehn-fillings along a fundamental shadow link complement, provided that their volumes are sufficiently close to that of the complement. More generally, we show that the conjectured asymptotic expansions hold for pairs obtained by change-of-pair operations on a fundamental shadow link complement whenever the volume of the corresponding hyperbolic cone manifold is sufficiently close to that of the complement. A key ingredient in the proof is the introduction of extended quantum $6j$-symbols and a Weak Reflection Symmetry satisfied by them. The Weak Reflection Symmetry is established by relating the extended quantum $6j$-symbols to the $b$-$6j$ symbols through a real Gevrey-$1$ estimate and a truncated Borel-Laplace transform.

papers.title: Zariski dense hyperbolic 3-manifold groups in $\mathrm{SL}(4,\mathbb{Z})$
papers.abstract: We show that $\mathrm{SL}(4,\mathbb{Z})$ contains an infinite family of Zariski-dense subgroups isomorphic to the fundamental group of a fixed closed hyperbolic $3$-manifold, which are pairwise noncommensurable up to conjugacy.

papers.title: Cable Knot Counterexamples to the All-Knot Volume Conjecture
papers.abstract: Let $E$ be the figure-eight knot and let $V$ be the hyperbolic volume of its exterior. We study the reduced colored Jones polynomial at $q=e^{2\pi i/N}$ for the $(p,w)$-cable of the connected sum of $d\ge 2$ copies of $E$, where $w\ge 2$ and $p,w$ are coprime. The normalized logarithmic growth rate converges to the JSJ volume $dV$ along colors coprime to $2w$, and its upper limit along colors sharing a divisor with $w$ is at most $V$. Thus the $(1,2)$-cable of $E\#E$ violates the full-sequence volume limit for knots. The $(1,3)$-cable of the same companion shows that convergence can fail even along all odd colors. The separation comes from the multiples of $N$ in the exact cabling sum and a uniform first-derivative estimate for the other companion colors.

papers.title: HOMFLY homology for oriented tangles
papers.abstract: We introduce an extension of Khovanov and Rozansky's categorification of the HOMFLY polynomial to arbitrary oriented tangles. Unlike previous such extensions, ours is invariant under the full suite of oriented Reidemeister moves, including the "misoriented" Reidemeister IIb. For oriented links $\mathcal{L}$, our construction recovers Khovanov and Rozansky's construction while removing the preliminary step of presenting $\mathcal{L}$ as a braid closure.

papers.title: Contact Surgery Numbers of the 3-torus
papers.abstract: We study contact surgery numbers for contact structures on the 3-torus. We show that all contact structures obtained via contact surgery along a Legendrian Borromean ring are overtwisted, and that this construction yields infinitely many pairwise non-contactomorphic contact structures on $\mathbb{T}^3$. We prove an obstruction on the maximal Thurston-Bennequin invariant of 3-component links to produce $\mathbb{T}^3$ by Dehn surgery. We also compare Legendrian surgery presentations of the Stein-fillable contact structure on $\mathbb{T}^3$. In this setting, we exhibit a non-destabilizable Legendrian knot with no graded normal ruling whose associated Stein filling has nonzero full symplectic homology.

papers.title: On the functoriality of the space of equivariant smooth $h$-cobordisms
papers.abstract: We construct an $(\infty,1)$-functor that takes each smooth $G$-manifold with corners $M$ to the space of equivariant smooth $h$-cobordisms ${\mathcal H}_{\mathrm{Diff}}(M)$. We also give a stable analogue ${\mathcal H}^{\mathcal U}_{\mathrm{Diff}}(M)$ where the manifolds are stabilized with respect to representation discs. The functor structure is subtle to construct, and relies on several new ideas. In the non-equivariant case $G=e$, our $(\infty,1)$-functor agrees with previous constructions of the smooth $h$-cobordism space as a functor to the homotopy category.

papers.title: Scl in graphs of groups
papers.abstract: Let G be a group acting on a tree with cyclic edge and vertex stabilizers. Then stable commutator length (scl) is rational in G. Furthermore, scl varies predictably and converges to rational limits in so-called "surgery" families. This is a homological analog of the phenomenon of geometric convergence in hyperbolic Dehn surgery.

papers.title: Holed cone structures on 3-manifolds
papers.abstract: We introduce holed cone structures on 3-manifolds to generalize cone structures. In the same way as a cone structure, a holed cone structure induces the holonomy representation. We consider the deformation space consisting of the holed cone structures on a 3-manifold whose holonomy representations are irreducible. This deformation space for positive cone angles is a covering space on a reasonable subspace of the character variety.

papers.title: The proper geometric dimension of the mapping class groups of non-orientable surfaces with punctures
papers.abstract: We study the proper geometric dimension of {\it full} mapping class groups of non-orientable surfaces with punctures. Building on the computation for closed non-orientable surfaces, we prove that the proper geometric dimension agrees with the virtual cohomological dimension in all but a finite collection of low-complexity cases, for which we obtain explicit bounds. Our results provide the non-orientable counterpart of the corresponding computations for mapping class groups of closed and punctured orientable surfaces.

papers.title: Chromatic Spherical and Renormalized Reshetikhin-Turaev Invariants for Drinfeld Centers
papers.abstract: We give invariants of pairs $(M,\Gamma)$ consisting of a closed connected oriented three-manifold and an oriented framed ribbon graph embedded in $M$ colored by the Drinfeld center of a unimodular finite chromatic category $\mathcal C$. This invariant generalizes the chromatic spherical and renormalized Reshetikhin-Turaev invariants of three-manifolds. We use Heegaard-Graph diagrams which represent the pair $(M,\Gamma)$ and use the data of a unimodular chromatic category and objects of the Drinfeld center to construct the invariant. We define a ribbon graph associated to embedded framed links to obtain an invariant of pairs $(M,L)$. We show that if $L$ is the empty link, then the invariant recovers the chromatic spherical invariant, and if $M$ is the three-sphere, then the invariant recovers the renormalized Reshetikhin-Turaev invariant from the Drinfeld center. The relationship is proven by recovering a chromatic structure for the center induced by that from $\mathcal C$. The main theorem of the paper demonstrates that if the graph is a link $L$ colored by a generator in the Drinfeld center, then we recover the chromatic spherical invariant of the surgery manifold $M(L)$, contributing to a proof of the relationship between the chromatic spherical and renormalized Reshetikhin-Turaev invariants for unimodular chromatic categories, generalizing a recent result for unimodular Hopf algebras by Reina. To this end, we give a Heegaard diagram for $M(L)$ coming from the Heegaard-Link diagram representing the pair $(M,L)$.
